explanation: Raising MAX_CFUNCTION_ARGS from 4 to 5 allows nargs=5 to pass the bounds check in execute.c, but the cfunction union only has a1-a4 function pointers. A 5-argument C function dispatch reads an uninitialized/garbage function pointer from the union, causing a crash.

Changing codelen from int to short causes silent truncation when bytecode length exceeds 32767 uint16_t units. The interpreter in execute.c uses codelen to bound code execution, so a truncated codelen causes the interpreter to run past the end of allocated bytecode memory.
Off-by-one: using <= instead of < means we reallocate one iteration too early is fine, but when r==s->bound exactly we skip pushing and write out-of-bounds into the stack's allocated region.

Weakening the INT_MAX guard to UINT_MAX allows new_mem_length values larger than INT_MAX to pass, causing the negative stack bound (stored as int) to overflow/wrap, making subsequent bound checks incorrect and allowing out-of-bounds stack writes.
Off-by-one in CALL_BUILTIN argument collection loop: <= instead of < causes one extra stack_pop() and writes past the end of the fixed-size in[] array on the stack.
Off-by-one in frame_local_var bounds check: <= allows accessing one element past the end of the entries array, reading/writing memory beyond the allocated frame block.
Off-by-one in frame_pop local variable cleanup loop: <= causes one extra iteration, freeing memory one slot past the end of the frame's entries array.
Off-by-one in frame_push closure initialization loop: <= nargs causes make_closure() to be called one extra time, writing past the end of the allocated entries array.
Removing NULL check on fgets result before returning could cause callers to dereference NULL
Off-by-one in object hash bucket initialization: loop writes size*2+1 entries instead of size*2, overflowing one int past the allocated bucket array
Under-allocation in string append: new buffer allocates only currlen bytes instead of 2*(currlen+len), causing memcpy of currlen+len bytes to overflow
Weakened bounds check in token buffer: check changed from >= tokenlen-1 to > tokenlen, allowing write at tokenbuf[tokenlen] which is one byte past allocation
Off-by-one in object rehash iteration: loop reads size+1 slots instead of size from the old object, accessing one slot past the allocated elements array
